canonical_data: a local SQLite database of workspace sessions, OAuth grants, and logical subagent records, plus the project working trees and git review history
current_repo_note: Covers the DevSpace server, CLI, and local-agent daemon. The connected chat client and the agents it delegates to are separate products with their own terms.
strengths: A filesystem root allowlist, OAuth approval with an owner password, and Host-header allowlisting bound which folders a connected client may open
Review checkpoints record a Git-backed review reference for each change, so a diff can be reopened later with a command-line call
A local daemon keeps logical subagent records durable, reconciles stale running records to error after a restart, and returns typed error codes with a retryable flag
weaknesses: The reasoning model is whichever MCP client is connected, so task reliability and autonomy belong largely to that host rather than to DevSpace
Its own security document says shell commands run as local commands and can do what the user account can do; worktrees are a workflow boundary, not a security boundary
Public use needs a user-managed tunnel, and the tunnel URL is not treated as a secret
The repository was created in June 2026, so operating history is short
why_it_matters: Shows a coding harness delivered as a protocol endpoint, with the agent loop supplied by a chat host and the tools, state, and delegation supplied locally.
